# deep :: rv_soybeans_state_2026_09_07

**Q:** what is the situation on soybeans now? how is it looking 3 months from now?

**TL;DR.** As of 2026-09-16 the CBOT soybean balance tilts modestly toward higher prices over the next three months: the US stocks-to-use buffer reads tight at 10.72% [N47] after three consecutive marketing years of decline, and the crush is paying well with a board crush of 2.6 USD/bu [N50] in the 92nd percentile of its own record [N52]  --  that demand-pull leg is the one I expect to dominate.

**Why.** ## Mechanism

The physical chain that matters into December runs through two legs that partly offset.

- **Tight balance sheet, price-supportive.** A lower US stocks-to-use ratio is a high-confidence inverse driver: less cushion per unit of use means any yield or demand surprise has to be rationed by price rather than by stocks. That is where the response turns convex  --  a thin buffer makes a supply shock right-tailed, while a big crop is capped by the same thin carryout, so the skew is asymmetric upward.
- **Crush demand pull, price-supportive.** Wide crush margins make processors bid aggressively for beans; the model ranks crush margin high-confidence and board crush medium, with a zero-to-one-quarter lag. Note these two are one series read under two names  --  one reading, not two.
- **Export pace and acreage, price-pressuring.** A slow US sales pace signals weak demand and rebuilds carryout (high confidence, zero to one quarter); larger area loosens supply with a two-to-four-quarter lag, and that acreage window sits inside the three-month horizon.
- **The ocean phase.** The tropical Pacific reading is carried under both phase names on one series; the driver model signs the warm phase as price-pressuring (medium confidence) through better South American rainfall, and the cool phase as price-supportive (high confidence). At +1.8 degC [N23] the phase in force is the warm one, and its stated effect window on beans closed 2026-05-30  --  so it is a watch item for the next South American season, not a driver inside the next three months.
- One lower-confidence channel is Thailand's food-grade quota pull, price-supportive at low confidence; treat it as a hypothesis, not a mechanism you lean on.

The model's own pattern count says the same thing as the drivers: the crush-led demand-pull pattern has three of its drivers among the loudest readings against a threshold of two, while the supply-glut pattern has two against a threshold of three, and the South American weather squeeze has one against three. That is why I lean price-supportive without calling it one-sided.

## The record

Levels read as of 2026-09-16, each on its own series:

- US stocks-to-use 10.72% [N47], -0.7 sigma on ten marketing years [N48], 23rd percentile of its own record [N49], falling three marketing years running  --  past the desk's own line for tight.
- Board crush 2.6 USD/bu [N50], 92nd percentile [N52], read through 2026-08-21, a 26-day span to this as-of; the same series under the crush-margin name reads 2.6 USD/bu [N50].
- Weekly export shipments 311.85 thousand MT [N38], -1.3 sigma on fifty-two weeks [N39], 6th percentile [N40], falling on the week.
- Managed money net long 234,920 contracts [N29], +2.0 sigma on three years [N30], 100th percentile of its own record [N31], rising three weeks running. This is what the reporting funds held, not a cause the model declares  --  it is the amplifier that can overextend a rally and the same reason a reversal, if one comes, is abrupt.
- Tropical Pacific +1.8 degC, +2.4 sigma on 120 months, 93rd percentile, rising eight months running.
- US area 34.76 M ha [N59], 91st percentile [N61]; Argentine production 50 MMT [N56], 85th percentile [N58]; Brazilian supply 118 MMT [N32], 99th percentile [N34]; Chinese stocks 44.36 MMT [N35], 98th percentile [N37], falling over the last marketing year. Flash-drought reading 0.6 z [N44], 85th percentile [N46].
- USDA's own numbers: 2025/26 ending stocks 325 million bushels [N7] on production of 4,262 million bushels [N8]; for 2026/27 USDA projects ending stocks of 310 million bushels [N19] on production of 4,535 million bushels [N20] and exports of 1,685 million bushels [N22], with a projected season-average farm price of 12 $/bu [N21] against 10.5 $/bu [N9] for 2025/26  --  those forward figures are USDA projections, not observed actuals and not mine. The March 2027 delivery settled at 1,328 US cents/bushel [N2].
- Dated documents, all older than the numbers: China's additional 10 percent tariff on US-origin soybeans took effect 2025-03-10 [E4], the channel the model signs as price-pressuring for the US board. Most recently, a 2026-04-17 report notes US soybean oil values trending higher on strong biofuel demand and firm crude [E39]  --  that is the demand-side leg behind the crush.
- Two of the three published stocks-to-use lookups returned nothing at all; the record carries no figure for those scopes and I assert none. The front delivery month could not be named on this session, so there is no "the price" on this page  --  only the named March 2027 delivery.
- No past state on this series is like the present one under the likeness rule, so there is no base-rate analogue to hand you here.

Older history, for framing only and not a forecast: on the 2011 analogue window the ocean reading was -0.68 degC [N79] against 1.8 degC [N80] now, with the US drought reading 0.90036 z [N81] then versus 2.24909 z [N82] now  --  the two are the opposite ocean phase, so do not read 2011 as a template. The settled USDA season-average farm price rose from $9.59/bu [N77] in MY2009/10 to $11.30/bu [N78] in MY2010/11; survey actuals, not futures.

On a 2015-10 to 2016-06 window, one delivery month held at both ends: CBOT soybeans +28.7976 % [N83] on the July 2016 delivery. The model records soybeans and Chinese rapeseed meal as competing for the same demand; over that window Chinese rapeseed meal was +29.037 % [N84] on its July 2016 delivery, and the declared relation held on this firing, in-sample on that window only  --  the direction is read on each board's own-currency move, US dollars and Chinese yuan, with no rate applied to either. The Chinese yuan per US dollar rate moved +3.9953 % [N85] from 2015-11-02 through 2016-06-17, carried as a dated fact on the rate itself. Chinese rapeseed oil, declared to compete for the same demand, was +7.4786 % [N86] on its July 2016 delivery, and that relation held on this firing too, again on own-currency moves in dollars and yuan. Soybeans and soybean meal are joined by the same crush; meal was +35.4388 % [N87], and that relation held. Meal against soybean oil is declared to compete for the same demand, and there the two moves sat at odds with the declared relation on this firing: soybean oil was +9.6121 % [N88]. MATIF rapeseed and CME palm oil each have no figure on this window because it predates those boards' own price history  --  a stated limit, not a zero. All of these are dated history: the window ended 2016-06-17, roughly a decade before this as-of.

## Where the record disagrees

The board leans both ways, and the two legs are not the same weight.

- Price-supportive, high confidence: the tight stocks-to-use buffer [N47] and a crush margin in the top decile of its own record [N52].
- Price-pressuring, high confidence: the export program sitting in the 6th percentile of its own record [N40]. A slow pace rebuilds the very carryout the tight ratio is measuring, which is why I call the setup two-sided rather than clean.
- The tiebreaker I use is the lag geometry, not a measured attribution: the export and crush windows both opened in August 2026 and close around November 2026, while the acreage-loosening window runs into December 2026 and the warm-phase ocean window already closed in May 2026. Inside three months the crush leg and the tight ratio are the live ones.
- One more honest split: the dated documents and the numbers disagree in vintage. The newest number carries a knowledge date of 20260904; the newest dated document behind this page is 2026-04-17. The tariff item [E4] is from March 2025 and must be read as history, not as a live shock.

## What to watch

- **Chinese soybean stocks, 44.36 MMT [N35]**  --  top decile of their own record and falling over the last marketing year. Reserve releases loosen the world sheet the CBOT benchmark prices off; accumulation tightens it, and the model commits no direction. It is also one of the two drivers that put the trade-war demand-loss pattern at its own threshold of two. This reads wrong if the next print returns the series to the middle of its own record.
- **US weekly export shipments, 311.85 thousand MT [N38]**  --  bottom decile and past the desk's own line for a lagging pace. This is the single clearest counterweight to the tight-balance read, and the model places it one hop upstream of both the stocks-to-use ratio and the WASDE revision that re-prices the sheet. Its declared window runs 2026-08-27 to 2026-11-27. It reads wrong if the next print returns to mid-record.
- **Board crush, 2.6 USD/bu [N50]**  --  four declared upstream paths (crude, the Renewable Fuel Standard, the biodiesel mandate, and one further cause) reach the bean price through this reading, so the demand-pull leg has more than one route in. Window 2026-08-20 to 2026-11-20. It reads wrong if those paths share one upstream cause, in which case it is one route counted twice, not four.
- **Crude, 0.51 z [N62]**  --  the same reading is declared on twenty-three other markets, twenty-two in the same direction; it is the through-line under the whole vegetable-oil-for-fuel bid, and its window runs 2026-08-01 to 2027-02-01. It reads wrong if the neighbouring market's own edge carries no sign, making the reach a count rather than a direction.
- **The tropical Pacific, +1.8 degC [N23]**  --  past the desk's line for a strong reading, eight months rising. Conditionally, counted from this reading's own date, its declared window opens around October 2026 and closes around January 2027: that is the South American growing season, and it is where the next real convexity sits. It reads wrong if the next print turns back inside that line or the run breaks.

The publishers' own scheduled print dates for these series are noted separately and are not watch items. Nothing else cleared the bar.

**Cascade / convergence**
